title: RAW natural appetite with sensory qualification and separate acquisition
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. Albertus distinguishes the natural appetite account from its sensed hunger/thirst form and from attraction. Candidate compositional content preserves the physiological need while qualifying sensory status; it supplies no target meanings.

design.question: Could one reusable qualification preserve an appetite description while explicitly changing its sensory status, without making desire a successful acquisition?
design.source_specific_content: The opening attributes natural appetite to nutritional vacancy and loss. In beings with sensitive and vegetative soul it also involves sensation, named hunger and thirst. The chapter separately explains attraction in plants and animals.
design.source_locus: Opening enumeration and following paragraph, current reader lines 24-25; attraction continuation lines 27-28 provides the action contrast.
design.unknown_after_source: Neither a target sensory qualifier nor a target natural-appetite expression has been found by this task. It is unknown whether shared written construction, distinct named terms, or a different content account is appropriate.

proposed_content_schema.base: APPETITE_DESCRIPTION(bearer, nutritional_deficit) states the selected source account of natural appetite; it does not assert food acquisition or bind a physical event merely from a kind name.
proposed_content_schema.qualification: WITH_SENSATION(appetite_description, explicit_sensory_status) preserves the appetite bearer and deficit description while adding the sensory qualification. Source linkage is at the appetite-kind level; token/event identity across two written descriptions requires a separate explicit reference.
proposed_content_schema.class_condition: The source applies the sensory account within beings with sensitive and vegetative soul. It does not confer sensitive powers on plants merely because plants have the natural appetite account.
proposed_content_schema.action_boundary: An independently expressed attraction/acquisition claim must retain its own event and instrument arguments. Appetite alone entails neither successful intake nor an animal-specific villus instrument.
proposed_content_schema.scope_caution: This is an analytical schema for the chapter, not an iff law saying every deficit is consciously felt at every moment; no sleep, intensity or species exception is invented.

connected_cases.input: A plant bearer with a stated nutritional deficiency
connected_cases.consequence: The natural-appetite description can be retained; the described sensitive-soul qualification cannot be inferred from that deficiency. Plant attraction, if asserted, requires its separately stated mechanism.

connected_cases.input: A bearer explicitly within the sensitive-plus-vegetative class, with a sensed evacuation description
connected_cases.consequence: The sensory qualification adds the hunger/thirst aspect to the natural-appetite account; successful attraction remains a separate assertion.

rivals.name: Distinct named appetite kinds
rivals.contract: Use independent terms for natural appetite and hunger/thirst, plus an explicit prose relationship. This can express the same source physiology.
rivals.distinguishing_consequence: A shared written appetite base with a stable sensory operator could constrain construction choice; source facts alone cannot distinguish these encodings.

rivals.name: Appetite is attraction
rivals.contract: Treat appetite and acquisition as one event predicate.
rivals.distinguishing_consequence: It loses the source separation between nutritional need or its sensation and the independently instrumented attraction operation. A full reading must state additional event content if it claims intake.

rivals.name: Universal sensory appetite
rivals.contract: Infer hunger/thirst sensation from nutritional deficiency for every vegetative bearer.
rivals.distinguishing_consequence: It incorrectly transfers the chapter's sensory qualification to the plant case without a stated sensitive-soul condition.

costs.unbound: All written bearers, class conditions, deficits, sensory arguments, event references and argument order. Two schemas are not assumed to be two words or morphemes.

design.minimum_next_step: First review the named predecessors for condition scope and faculty nominalization. Only if a distinction remains, author one complete admitted passage containing natural and qualified appetite accounts plus their written bearers; keep all alternate reader forms explicit. No executor before these bindings exist.
design.decision_changing_result: A shared construction that preserves the need/bearer account under sensory qualification while requiring separate attraction content could favor this reusable content hypothesis. If only independent named terms express the same facts, the construction remains unchosen; if sensation must be silently projected to plants or desire must mean successful intake, reject that authored descendant.
assumptions: The chapter's account is a possible content source, not an identified exemplar.
Sensory qualification is proposed compositional content; the source does not prescribe a target grammar.
No physiological class, appetite word or action word is inherited from old drafts.
